option_relations.rationale: The patient's known plexiform neurofibroma and bilateral vestibular schwannomas are characteristic of Neurofibromatosis type 2.
There is no indication of thrombophilia in the patient's laboratory results or clinical presentation.
The patient's laboratory results do not suggest an autoimmune vasculitis, and the clinical presentation is not consistent with this diagnosis.
There is no indication of an infectious cause in the patient's laboratory results or clinical presentation.
The patient's carotid Doppler ultrasound was normal, making an embolic source from carotid artery disease unlikely.
The patient's transthoracic echocardiography was normal, making a cardiac embolic source unlikely.
There is no indication of Moyamoya syndrome in the patient's laboratory results or clinical presentation.
The patient denied the use of any drugs that could be related to the clinical presentation.
